title: Beyond the 956: Brian Ahern, legendary producer behind Emmylou Harris and Anne Murray, dies at 81
excerpt: Brian Ahern, the Canadian producer who shaped the sound of Emmylou Harris and Anne Murray, died November 9, 2026, at 81 in Minnesota. He was inducted into the Canadian Country Music Hall of Fame in 2006 and named a Member of the Order of Canada in 2019.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Brian Ahern, the Canadian record producer whose work behind the mixing board shaped the solo careers of Emmylou Harris and Anne Murray, has died at 81.

Ahern died Monday, November 9, 2026, in Minnesota, according to MusicRow and the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum, which remembered his work in a statement. No cause of death was publicly disclosed.

Born in Halifax, Nova Scotia, in 1945, Ahern began playing guitar professionally as a teenager and became one of the most respected producers in country and Americana music. He produced 11 albums for Emmylou Harris between 1975 and 1983, including Pieces of the Sky, Elite Hotel, Luxury Liner and Roses in the Snow, and reunited with her for 2008's All I Intended to Be. He also produced 12 albums for Anne Murray, including her 1969 breakthrough This Way Is My Way and its hit “Snowbird.”

His credits also included records for Johnny Cash, Willie Nelson, George Jones, Roy Orbison, Glen Campbell, Don Williams and Linda Ronstadt. He built the Enactron Truck, a mobile recording studio that let him record artists on location.

Ahern and Harris were married from 1977 to 1984 and had a daughter, Meghann. He was inducted into the Canadian Country Music Hall of Fame in 2006, received a Lifetime Achievement Award for Producer/Engineer from the Americana Music Association in 2010, and was named a Member of the Order of Canada in 2019.

In its statement, the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum said Ahern's work “helped create an essential form of American roots music” that continues to inspire artists today. Funeral arrangements were not immediately announced.

Sources: MusicRow; Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum; American Songwriter; Roots Music Canada.
